棺.meaning: A vampire <part>bureaucrat</part> sleeps all day in a long box carved from one old oak <part>tree</part>, with a 'Do Not Disturb' form stamped on the lid in triplicate. At sunset he climbs out, straightens his tie and goes to file papers. His bed is a <kanji>coffin</kanji>.
棺.on: He pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to his cape before work.

肘.meaning: An astronaut tries a <part>golf club</part> swing on the <part>moon</part>, but her stiff suit won't bend halfway along her arm. Whoosh: she misses the ball, spins and floats over. Back at base she fits a hinge to the suit's weak spot: the <kanji>elbow</kanji>.
肘.on: She blows a bubble of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum as she tightens the screws.
肘.kun: In the <sound>hea</sound>t of the sun the hinge works fine, and she drives off in her moon <sound>jee</sound>p.

虎.meaning: A <part>tiger</part> painted on a circus banner gets bored, grows a pair of <part>legs</part> and steps right off the canvas, still flat as paper. It prowls the ring and roars like a rustling page, and the crowd claps anyway for the paper <kanji>tiger</kanji>.
虎.on: Then it curls up to nap beside a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala in the next tent.
虎.kun: The koala offers it a <sound>to</sound>ffee and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

藩.meaning: On a small island, every family takes its <part>turn</part> to guard the well: they cover it with cut <part>grass</part> against the sun and count the <part>water drops</part> so nobody takes more than their share. Hundreds of cousins, one well, one rule: they are a <kanji>clan</kanji>.
藩.on: Whoever guards the well gets a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey as thanks.

伎.meaning: A hiker hangs her jacket on a <part>coat hook</part> by a stream, snaps a <part>branch</part> off a willow and whittles it into a tiny boat for a crying boy who lost his toy in the water. No badge for it, no photo, just a good <kanji>deed</kanji>.
伎.on: The boy gives her a big brass <sound>key</sound> to his treehouse in return.
伎.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>, hu<sound>zzah</sound>!' he cheers, as the little boat sails off: a real skill.

諦.meaning: The <part>emperor</part> bans every <part>speech</part> that isn't flattering. One day his parrot, who never learned to flatter, squawks, 'Your crown is crooked!' The court gasps; the emperor checks a mirror and laughs. At last someone told him the <kanji>truth</kanji>.
諦.on: He fixes the crown straight with a strip of sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
諦.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' he sighs, giving up on flattery, and shares a <sound>ki</sound>wi and some <sound>ra</sound>men with the parrot.

謙.meaning: A famous opera singer is giving two shows <part>concurrently</part>: one for the grand hall, one for a single janitor sweeping backstage. She stops her big <part>speech</part>, walks down and sits on his bucket to sing just for him. A star happy to come down to anyone's level: she will <kanji>condescend</kanji>.
謙.on: Her little dog howls along from his <sound>ken</sound>nel in the wings.
謙.kun: Afterwards she bows low to the <sound>herri</sound>ng seller, the <sound>coo</sound>k and the <sound>du</sound>ck that lives by the stage door.

畔.meaning: A farmer cuts her <part>rice field</part> in <part>half</part> with a raised strip of mud, so the ducks on the left can't squabble with the ducks on the right. Every morning she walks along its narrow top like a tightrope, arms out. The ducks call it the wall; she calls it the <kanji>paddy ridge</kanji>.
畔.on: Halfway along she stops to dip a finger in a pot of <sound>hon</sound>ey.
畔.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasps, as a <sound>ze</sound>ppelin drifts low over the ridge and the ducks all duck.

礁.meaning: An undersea volcano spits out a <part>stone</part> so hot its edges <part>char</part> black, and it cools into a jagged lump just under the waves. Ships steer round it, coral grows over it, and by spring a family of little fish has opened a café on it: the new <kanji>reef</kanji>.
礁.on: Every evening the clownfish put on a <sound>show</sound> there for passing turtles.
